gaps.spec_claim: Returns None when no codegraph index is available for the project, signaling backend unavailability so callers apply the regex-based fallback extractor to C++ files; the empty mapping is NOT returned in this case. When the index is available, returns a mapping in which every key is the absolute path of an indexed C++ source file and each value is the complete, position-ordered list of (function_name, body_text) pairs for that file: names carry the canonicalized in-file deduplication identity shared with extraction and call-graph construction, and each body text spans exactly the indexed line range of that function. Returns an empty mapping only when the index is available and contains no C++ functions.
gaps.actual_behavior:
The function returns a dict and does not raise any exception. There are two mutually exclusive cases:

1. (Index found) If a codegraph index database exists at proj_dir/.codegraph/codegraph.db or at the corresponding relative location under the parent of proj_dir, then CodeGraphExtractor.from_proj_dir(proj_dir) returns a valid extractor cg (not None). In this case the function returns cg.get_functions_by_file("cpp", proj_dir), which is a dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]] whose keys are the absolute paths of all C++ source files present in the index and whose values are, for each file, the complete position-ordered list of (deduplicated function identifier, body text) pairs. Each identifier follows the canonicalization and per-file deduplication identity shared by extraction and call-graph construction; each body text covers exactly the indexed line range of that function. Because the pre-condition guarantees the index was built against the current working tree, the returned file paths and line ranges are consistent with the on-disk sources.

2. (No index) If no codegraph index database exists at either location, CodeGraphExtractor.from_proj_dir(proj_dir) returns None. In this case the function returns the empty dict {}.

Formally:
  let idx_exists  ( db at proj_dir/.codegraph/codegraph.db)  ( db at parent(proj_dir)/.codegraph/codegraph.db)
  result = batch_extract(proj_dir)
  (idx_exists  result = {abs_path: [(fname, body), ...] | abs_path  indexed_cpp_files}   abs_path  result: result[abs_path] is position-ordered, deduplicated, and body spans the indexed line range)
   (idx_exists  result = {})
   isinstance(result, dict)
   no exception is raised
gaps.code_evidence: Line 4: return cg.get_functions_by_file("cpp", proj_dir) if cg else {}
gaps.trigger_condition: The specification (Condition B) explicitly states: 'Returns None when no codegraph index is available for the project, signaling backend unavailability so callers apply the regex-based fallback extractor to C++ files; the empty mapping is NOT returned in this case.' and 'Returns an empty mapping only when the index is available and contains no C++ functions.' However, the code returns {} (empty dict) when cg is None (no index found), instead of returning None. This means callers cannot distinguish between 'no index available' (should trigger regex fallback) and 'index available but no C++ functions' (legitimate empty result). The else branch on Line 4 should yield None, not {}.
